monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp drop in volume and intensity compared to last month, with only one run completed so far — significantly below the previous month’s activity level. While aerobic efficiency and cadence remain stable, the near-absence of higher-intensity work (Z4/Z5) and reduced run frequency signal an early-month stall.
monthly_review.highlight: The runner has completed only 1 run in May (4.6 km), representing just 12% of last month’s volume — the most notable finding is the abrupt drop in training consistency entering this month.

goal_tracker.message: You need 33.4 more km across 8 additional sessions in the remaining 29 days — averaging ~4.2 km per session — to match last month’s total distance and run count.

insights.title: Slight decline in efficiency despite stable VO2 max
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency dropped from 13.66 to 13.57 m/sec per bpm, while VO2 max increased from 35.0 to 36.0 — suggesting improved cardiovascular capacity but less effective translation into movement economy, possibly due to reduced stride length (85.17 cm vs prior 88.65–91.78 cm) and higher ground contact time (301 ms vs recent 298–327 ms range).

insights.title: Near-total absence of Zone 4–5 work this month
insights.body: This month’s HR zone distribution shows 0% in Z5 and only 2% in Z4 — down sharply from last month’s 4% Z5 and 15% Z4 — indicating loss of high-intensity stimulus critical for maintaining pace resilience and lactate tolerance.

insights.title: Cadence and stride length divergence
insights.body: Cadence dropped from 142 spm (Apr) to 133 spm (May), while stride length fell to 85.17 cm — yet vertical oscillation decreased (7.4 cm vs Apr avg ~7.7 cm) and ground contact time remained low (301 ms). This suggests a more cautious, shorter-stride pattern possibly linked to fatigue or reduced neuromuscular readiness.

insights.title: Low HR and long-slow run on 2026-04-26 signals active recovery use
insights.body: The 4.1 km run on 2026-04-26 had avg HR of 120 bpm, cadence of 87 spm, and pace of 14:00 min/km — well below typical Z1 effort and consistent with true recovery; however, no similar session appears scheduled this month, risking accumulation of residual fatigue.

recommendations.action: Do a 5 km Zone 2 run at avg HR ≤140 bpm tomorrow (2026-05-03), using cadence ≥140 spm as a real-time form cue
recommendations.reason: Your May avg cadence (133 spm) is 9 spm below April’s (142 spm), and Zone 2 HR is well-supported by your current avg HR of 139 bpm — this rebuilds rhythm without overstressing recovery.

recommendations.action: Insert one 6-minute Zone 3 interval session before May 15: 3 × 2-min @ avg HR 150–158 bpm with 90-sec walk recovery
recommendations.reason: Last month included 26% Z3 work and 4% Z5 — reintroducing short, controlled Z3 bouts will re-establish lactate buffering without requiring full hard efforts.

recommendations.action: After your next run, perform 3 × 60-sec single-leg balance holds (eyes open) + 2 × 10 slow calf raises per leg
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time has ranged 298–327 ms recently, and stride length declined — targeted neuromuscular activation supports elastic return and stride stability.

weekly_focus.description: Reestablish consistent cadence, controlled HR engagement, and neuromuscular coordination to reverse the early-month dip in volume and form metrics.
suggested_sessions: 5 km Zone 2 tempo (HR ≤140 bpm, cadence ≥140 spm)
3 × 2-min Zone 3 intervals (HR 150–158 bpm) with walk recovery
30-min easy run + mobility drill set (balance + calf focus)
